before.permit: North Cascades NP complex: no permit for day climbs; all overnight backcountry stays require a backcountry permit (reserve on Recreation.gov or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center).

climate.fall: Rain returns and temperatures drop; road access can still be fine into October.
climate.spring: Wet, with lingering snow on the access road into May/early June.
climate.summer: Warmest, driest window and the best time for rock climbing on this line.
climate.winter: Heavy snowfall typically makes Hannegan Pass Road impassable to vehicles; this is when climbers use the wall for dry-tooling.
climate.typical: Wet, temperate maritime climate with heavy winter snowfall and a relatively short dry-and-mild summer window.
climate.forecastZone: North Cascades / Mt. Baker area (western Whatcom County)

road.name: Hannegan Pass Road (FS-32), just off Mt. Baker Highway (SR-542) near milepost 46
road.status: Unpaved but easily accessible — the crag is only about 2 minutes' drive up Hannegan Pass Road from the highway turnoff.
road.driveNote: Roughly 2-2.5 hours from Seattle/Bellingham via SR-542 to the Hannegan Pass Road turnoff.
road.seasonalGate: Closed to vehicles Nov 1 – Mar 31 under an annual Forest Service closure order
